title: America Can Do Good—and Do Well
gist: Former USAID administrator Andrew Natsios argues DOGE's 2025 dismantling of USAID destroyed US foreign-aid capacity (est. 700,000+ excess deaths, more conflict), that shifting aid to State has produced unaccountable government-to-government transfers with transactional strings, and proposes a new cabinet-level aid department with field missions, fewer congressional committees, fewer earmarks and deregulated 'charter missions'.

themes.theme: Human and security toll of USAID's dismantling

insights.claim: A Lancet study found USAID's assistance prevented more than 90 million deaths between 2001 and 2021.
insights.speaker: Andrew Natsios
insights.so_what: Quantifies the scale of the US aid footprint that has been removed.
insights.quote: prevented more than 90 million deaths between 2001 and 2021

insights.claim: Boston University epidemiologist Brooke Nichols estimated that the 2025 dismantling of USAID contributed to more than 700,000 excess deaths over roughly a year.
insights.speaker: Andrew Natsios
insights.so_what: Humanitarian shock in aid-dependent countries raises instability and migration risk.
insights.quote: contributed to more than 700,000 excess deaths over roughly a year

insights.claim: A study in Science found that places losing large amounts of USAID assistance after the shutdown saw a marked uptick in armed clashes and riots, and Nicolini and Sabatini showed economic activity in formerly aid-heavy areas declined dramatically.
insights.speaker: Andrew Natsios
insights.so_what: Aid withdrawal is a measurable driver of conflict and economic contraction in frontier markets.
insights.quote: experienced a marked uptick in armed clashes and riots

insights.claim: After 90% of USAID's programs were terminated and 90% of its staff laid off, annual US foreign aid disbursements fell by $26 billion between FY2023-24 and FY2024-25 (Pew), and $2.5 billion in appropriated aid went unspent by end of FY2025-26 as OMB withheld funds.
insights.speaker: Andrew Natsios
insights.so_what: Even reappropriated money is not flowing; the delivery machinery is gone.
insights.quote: annual U.S. foreign aid disbursements fell by $26 billion
insights.locator: No country can be a great power

insights.claim: Natsios argues DOGE's stated goals of cutting waste were not realized, since Trump's 2025 'big beautiful bill' erased any modest savings from the foreign-aid cuts.
insights.speaker: Andrew Natsios
insights.so_what: Aid cuts were fiscally immaterial — the cost was strategic, not a budget win.
insights.quote: erased any modest savings won by DOGE’s cuts to foreign aid

insights.claim: Natsios asserts no country can be a great power without a functioning foreign aid program, and the United States currently does not have one, while China races to offer alternative development financing and Russia expands security partnerships.
insights.speaker: Andrew Natsios
insights.so_what: Vacuum benefits Chinese development finance and Russian security deals in the Global South.
insights.quote: No country can be a great power without a functioning foreign aid program.
insights.locator: No country can be a great power

themes.theme: State Department takeover: unaccountable, transactional aid

insights.claim: Moving USAID functions to the State Department has led to $3.8 billion transferred to UN OCHA and $15.9 billion paid directly into foreign governments' treasuries via memorandums of understanding.
insights.speaker: Andrew Natsios
entities: UN Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs
insights.so_what: Shift from audited project aid to budget transfers increases leakage risk.
insights.quote: $15.9 billion directly into foreign governments’ treasuries through memorandums of understanding
insights.locator: And the decision to move USAID’s functions

insights.claim: Over 90% of the countries receiving these State Department transfers score below 50 out of 100 on Transparency International's Corruption Perceptions Index, and political appointees have kept the agreement texts secret.
insights.speaker: Andrew Natsios
insights.so_what: High corruption risk for US funds; possible future scandal/oversight fights.
insights.quote: Over 90 percent of the countries involved in these agreements score below 50
insights.locator: These governments often have limited capacity

insights.claim: In exchange for 36 health-aid MOUs, Washington has asked recipient governments to share private health-care data, accept deported undocumented immigrants, and in some cases give US mining companies access to rare-earth minerals.
insights.speaker: Andrew Natsios
insights.so_what: Aid is being used as leverage for critical-mineral access — watch US miners gaining African/Asian rare-earth concessions.
insights.quote: give U.S. mining companies access to their rare-earth minerals
insights.locator: The State Department has pursued alternative

insights.claim: A September 2026 GAO audit found State lacked documented standards for terminating aid programs, could not produce data on its own staffing, and kept incomplete or incorrect grant records.
insights.speaker: Andrew Natsios
insights.so_what: Confirms operational failure of the post-USAID setup.
insights.quote: could not produce data on its own staffing

insights.claim: Natsios argues merging USAID into State makes as much sense as merging Microsoft with ExxonMobil, because diplomacy and development operate on different time horizons, missions and business systems.
insights.speaker: Andrew Natsios
insights.so_what: Expect continued dysfunction until aid is re-separated institutionally.
insights.quote: makes as much sense as merging Microsoft with ExxonMobil

insights.claim: OMB director Russell Vought has stonewalled democracy-support spending and insisted humanitarian grants go only to two specific Christian NGOs, while Marco Rubio sought to end funding to contractors, universities and local civil society groups.
insights.speaker: Andrew Natsios
insights.so_what: Ideological gating narrows the implementing ecosystem; development contractors lose business.
insights.quote: humanitarian grants can be sent only to two specific Christian nongovernmental organizations

themes.theme: Why aid underdelivered: counterbureaucracy and earmarks

insights.claim: Natsios argues USAID's much-criticized bureaucracy was actually an adaptation to manage conflicting demands that aid relieve misery, serve US military/diplomatic interests, and yield rapid, visible, quantifiable results.
insights.speaker: Andrew Natsios
insights.so_what: Abolishing process without replacement creates more waste, not less.
insights.quote: USAID’s bureaucracy, so often presented as an obstacle to effectiveness, was in fact an adaptation to manage these conflicts

insights.claim: USAID reported to 14 congressional committees, and in 2001 its funds were bound by nearly 250 earmarks totaling more than its entire appropriation, leaving no discretionary money to answer country requests.
insights.speaker: Andrew Natsios
insights.so_what: Structural rigidity, not agency incompetence, drove poor responsiveness.
insights.quote: nearly 250 congressional earmarks, a sum exceeding USAID’s total appropriation

insights.claim: In 2007 only 1.5% of USAID's budget went to agricultural development, 1.5% to economic growth and 1.5% to governance reform, even as Ethiopia was among the world's most food-insecure countries.
insights.speaker: Andrew Natsios
insights.so_what: Illustrates misallocation away from institution building.

insights.claim: Natsios argues institution building and policy reform should be the focus of aid because strong institutions separate rich from poor countries, but Washington's demand for quick visible results pushed USAID toward unsustainable service delivery.
insights.speaker: Andrew Natsios
insights.so_what: Long-horizon governance aid is the higher-return use of funds.
insights.quote: Institution building and policy reform should be the focus of aid programs.

insights.claim: USAID's Nixon-era shift to 50% of its budget on agriculture, mostly in Asia, fueled the green revolution, which studies credit with saving more than 245 million lives and generating grain surpluses that fed industrialization in countries like India, Indonesia, South Korea and Taiwan.
insights.speaker: Andrew Natsios
insights.so_what: Historical evidence that aid can underpin emerging-market growth and Cold War strategic wins.
insights.quote: the effort saved more than 245 million lives
insights.locator: In fact, USAID ended up playing

insights.claim: Studies show USAID Office of Transition Initiatives community projects in Iraq employed young men who might otherwise join militias, reducing US military casualties in the most violent provinces; DOGE abolished OTI.
insights.speaker: Andrew Natsios
insights.so_what: Aid cuts can raise military costs elsewhere.
insights.quote: reducing U.S. military casualties in the provinces with the highest levels of violence

themes.theme: Blueprint for a new US aid department

insights.claim: Natsios proposes Congress create a new cabinet-level department reporting to the president to manage all US aid programs, with at least 80% of staff deployed abroad and re-established country missions reporting to ambassadors.
insights.speaker: Andrew Natsios
insights.so_what: Potential policy agenda for the new Democratic Congress; watch for aid-reorganization legislation.
insights.quote: At least 80 percent of this new department’s staff should be deployed abroad

insights.claim: Natsios recommends the new aid department report only to a foreign affairs authorizing committee and an appropriations subcommittee in each chamber, with fewer domestic earmarks.
insights.speaker: Andrew Natsios
insights.so_what: Streamlined oversight would speed disbursement if enacted.
insights.locator: This new department should also report

insights.claim: Natsios proposes deregulated 'charter missions', modeled on charter schools, freed from counterbureaucracy reporting requirements, citing World Bank experience that a similar approach improved effectiveness without increasing fraud.
insights.speaker: Andrew Natsios
insights.so_what: A testable reform model; signals direction for future aid governance.
insights.quote: charter missions, similar to charter schools

insights.claim: Natsios argues Washington cannot simply revert to the old USAID status quo, and that the new Democratic Congress and future administrations have an opening to reform aid.
insights.speaker: Andrew Natsios
insights.so_what: Aid restoration likely to be partial and restructured, not a return to pre-2025 USAID.
insights.quote: Washington cannot revert to the old status quo
insights.locator: The status quo for U.S. foreign aid
